title: Plans — the future tense
title_target: আমি সিলেটে যাব — a-mi si-lé-Té ja-bô
goal: Talk about plans and promises with the -ব ending, and build simple conditional sentences with যদি — “if …, then …”.
bekal: forming the future: করব, যাব, খাব, থাকব

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Planning a trip to Sylhet
dialogs.intro: Ani wants to see the tea gardens in Sylhet before she goes home. Rahim helps her make a plan. Watch the -ব ending, which marks that none of it has happened yet.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I want to go to Sylhet. How do I get there?
lines.literal: I — Sylhet-to — go-to — want. how — will-go?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Take the train. It's comfortable, and cheap too.
lines.literal: train-by — go. comfort-with — will-go, and — cheap-too.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: How long does the trip take?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: About seven hours. If you take the night train, you'll arrive in the morning.
lines.literal: about — seven — hours. night-of — train-by — if-go — morning-in — will-arrive.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Where do I get a ticket?

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Buy it online. I'll get it for you tonight.
lines.literal: online-on — will-cut. I — today — night-at — cut — will-give.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: If I get leave, I'll come. If not, Mitali will go.
lines.literal: if — leave — get, then — will-go. if-not — Mitali — will-go.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Tea gardens, waterfalls, and the haor. In the rainy season the haor becomes like a sea.
lines.literal: tea — garden, waterfall, and — haor. rainy-season-in — haor — sea-of — like — becomes.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: A huge wetland. You'll go around by boat. You'll never forget it.
lines.literal: vast — water-land. boat-by — will-go-around. will-forget — not — any-day.

notes: **The future uses the -ব ending, with a set of forms parallel to the ones you know:** **-ব** for আমি, **-বে** for তুমি, **-বেন** for আপনি, **-বে** for সে. করা → করব · করবে · করবেন · করবে. ⚠️ Note that **তুমি and সে share exactly the same form** — করবে for both. Bengali lets context decide, and in real conversation that's never a problem.

**The stem doesn't change at all, even for verbs that are irregular in the past.** যাওয়া → **যাব** (not *গেব*), আসা → **আসব**, খাওয়া → **খাব**, দেওয়া → **দেব**, নেওয়া → **নেব**, পাওয়া → **পাব**, হওয়া → **হব**. ⚠️ So if the past gave you a headache in Unit 13, the future will come as a relief.

**The -বেন form you learned in Unit 17 as a gentle request is exactly the same form.** আপনি যাবেন can mean “you will go” or “please go”, and the tone decides. ⚠️ No coincidence: many languages use the future to be polite — compare English “Will you sit down?”.

**Conditional sentences are built with যদি … তাহলে ….** যদি বৃষ্টি হয়, তাহলে যাব না (if it rains, I won't go). যদি সময় পাই, তাহলে আসব (if I have time, I'll come). ⚠️ The verb in the first part usually takes the **present**, not the future — just as English says “if it rains”, not “if it will rain”.

**There's a shortcut for conditions: the -লে ending.** গেলে (if you go), খেলে (if you eat), হলে (if it becomes), পেলে (if you get). রাতের ট্রেনে **গেলে** সকালে পৌঁছাবেন = “if you take the night train, you'll arrive in the morning”. It's shorter and more common than যদি. ⚠️ It looks like the তুমি past (গেলে = you went), so watch the sentence structure.
**নাহলে *nahôlé* means “otherwise” and is very handy.** এখনই যান, নাহলে দেরি হবে (go now, otherwise you'll be late). On its own it also means “or”: চা নাহলে কফি (tea or coffee).

⚠️ **লঞ্চ — a river ferry — is a vehicle with no real equivalent in everyday English.** Bangladesh is a land of rivers, and an overnight লঞ্চ trip from Dhaka to the south is an experience like no other. Other useful words: **নৌকা** *nouka* (small boat), **ঘাট** *ghaT* (landing, river steps), **হাওর** *haôr* (a vast wetland that turns into a sea in the rainy season).

grammars.title: The future — ভবিষ্যৎ কাল
after: **The negative is still না at the end:** আমি যাব না (I won't go), সে আসবে না (he/she won't come), আমি পারব না (I won't be able to).
⚠️ **আমি পারব না is the politest way to say no** — “I won't be able to”. Far softer than “I don't want to”, and almost never questioned.

grammars.title: If … then …

head: বাংলা
Say it
Meaning
rows: যদি বৃষ্টি হয়, তাহলে যাব না।
jô-di brish-Ti hôy, ta-hô-lé ja-bô na
If it rains, I won't go.
If I have time, I'll come.
If you take the train, you'll arrive in the morning.
If you're late, give me a call.
Go now, otherwise you'll be late.
If you like it, I'll come again.

after: **তাহলে can be dropped** when the structure is already clear: যদি সময় পাই, আসব. In fast speech people more often use just the -লে ending and drop যদি entirely.

sections.title: Traveling in a land of rivers

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: Does this train go to Sylhet?

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three things about traveling in Bangladesh
items: **Train tickets sell out far in advance, especially before Eid.** The phrase for buying a ticket is **টিকিট কাটা** — literally “to cut a ticket”, from the days of torn paper tickets. Don't be puzzled by the word “cut”.

**Rivers are highways.** Bangladesh has more than seven hundred rivers, and the overnight লঞ্চ from Dhaka to Barisal is a trip people talk about for life. ⚠️ In storm season, watch the weather announcements; river trips are sometimes canceled, and that's for your safety.

**The season decides everything.** **বর্ষা** *bôrsha* (the rainy season, June–September) transforms the landscape: wetlands become seas, roads become rivers, and overland travel slows down. **শীত** *shit* (winter, December–February) is the best time to travel — cool, dry, and full of festivals.

blocks.text: One word worth taking home: **ঘাট** *ghaT*. It means the stone steps leading down to a river — where people bathe, wash, tie up boats, sit in the afternoon, and see people off. In Bengal's towns the ghat is the real public space, and sitting there watching the river counts as a perfectly legitimate activity. If you want to see Bengali life without buying any ticket, go to a ghat around sunset.

exercises.prompt: Change into the future for আমি.
Put the words in the right order.

items: How long does the trip take?
If I have time, I'll come.
I won't be able to today.
Does this train go to Dhaka?

আমি সিলেটে যাব। — কত সময় লাগবে? — যদি সময় পাই, আসব। — আজ আমি পারব না। — এই ট্রেন কি ঢাকা যায়? — কখন ছাড়বে?
